Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

 5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine attended the Community Connection & Clean-up, the 17th annual
  Walk of Life for the Armenian Bone Marrow Registry, GPD’s Faith in Blue, the Philippine
  History Month celebration, and the YWCA Racial Justice event. She thanked everyone
  involved for making these events a success. Devine asked staff to provide a report on in-home
  businesses and the traffic situation along Glenoaks and Carmel. City Manager Roubik
  Golanian indicated that Public Works Director Yazdan Emrani is aware of the traffic and safety
  situation and has directed staff to look into how the city can improve traffic and pedestrian
  safety around the Glenoaks Elementary area. Emrani provided his comments and indicated
  that staff will provide a report in a few weeks.

  Councilmember Asatryan noted that in addition to the events noted by Councilmember Devine
  she attended Imagine Theatre’s Gala along with Councilmember Brotman. The Imagine
  Theatre, based in Glendale, introduces young people to live theater and coordinates with the
  school district. She invited the public to their next production “Warrior Queen: Anahit the
  Brave”. Asatryan invited the public to attend the Artsakh Paseo's Concert Series held every
  Saturday at 5pm. Asatryan noted that she has been made aware that health insurance rates
  for city employees have significantly increased and we need to take action to help relieve the
  unexpected financial burden placed along with the inflation. Provided that the current
  agreement with the city’s broker who secured the rates expires 2024, Asatryan commented
  that she would like to re-release an RFP and asked staff to come back with a report and an
  RFP to obtain a new broker who may get better rates. Brotman seconded. Golanian provided
  his comments and indicated that staff will provide a report and an RFP as soon as possible.

  Councilmember Brotman asked staff to provide a report on housing related bills such as AB-
  2097, AB-2011 and SB-379. Golanian indicated that staff will bring a report to council.

  Mayor Pro Tem Najarian announced that Metro opened the new K line light rail which will
  travel from downtown LA to LAX Airport. He accepted two awards on behalf of LA Metro and
  Metrolink on sustainability from the American Public Transportation Association.

  Director of Community Development Bradley Calvert announced the return of Glendale Tech
  Week from October 15-20.
